Title: Bursa Malaysia stays lower at midday
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia remained lower at midday, weighed down by selling pressure in selected heavyweights, particularly the plantation, financial services and utility counters.
At 12.30 pm, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) slid 5.63 points, or 0.32 per cent, to 1,735.98 from Wednesday's close of 1,741.61.
The benchmark index opened 1.18 points higher at 1,742.79, and fluctuated between 1,733.21 and 1,742.79 during the morning trading session.
On the broader market, losers outpaced gainers 601 to 357, while 539 counters were unchanged, 1,301 untraded and 15 suspended.
Turnover totalled 1.90 billion units worth RM1.30 billion.
In a note today, Apex Securities Bhd said utilities and energy counters may extend their gains, supported by continued buying momentum and firm crude oil prices.
"Construction could remain resilient, supported by sustained data centre and artificial intelligence (AI)-related investments, which should underpin job flows and earnings visibility for selected contractors," it said.
Among the heavyweights, CIMB Group gained four sen to RM7.96, while Maybank shed two sen to RM10.58, Public Bank eased three sen to RM5.16, IHH Healthcare slid four sen each to RM5.15 and Tenaga Nasional was six sen lower to RM14.52.
On the most active list, Key ASIC added three sen to 6.5 sen, Ekovest was half a sen higher at 20.5 sen, Oppstar rose three sen to 71.5 sen, and HHRG inched up half a sen to 16 sen, while NationGate eased three sen to RM1.53.
Of the top gainers, Nestle surged RM1.40 to RM104.30, Malaysian Pacific Industries rose 52 sen to RM48.02, UMS Integration gained 19 sen to RM8.34, Ideal Capital firmed 18 sen to RM3.68, and Kee Ming Group put on 15 sen to RM2.28.
As for the top losers, Hong Leong Bank fell 34 sen to RM22.36, United Plantations slid 28 sen to RM33.32, PPB Group dropped 17 sen to RM9.36, Malaysia Smelting Corporation lost 16 sen to RM2.06 and Fraser & Neave erased 14 sen to RM26.76.
On the index board, the FBM ACE Index advanced 40.73 points to 5,244.16, while the FBM Emas Index eased 41.29 points to 12,877.41, and the FBMT 100 Index slid 39.01 points to 12,6789.82.
The FBM Emas Shariah Index fell 49.31 points to 12,721.57 and the FBM 70 Index gave up 47.21 points to 18,388.60.
By sector, the Energy Index edged up 1.06 points to 786.80, while the Financial Services Index gave up 45.87 points to 20,354.15, the Plantation Index slipped 84.38 points to 9,383.96, and the Industrial Products and Services Index edged down 0.56 points to 189.79.

Title: Malaysia's natural rubber output jumps 31.5pct in June
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's natural rubber (NR) production rose 31.5 per cent month-on-month to 26,553 tonnes in June from 20,198 tonnes in May, according to the Statistics Department.
On a year-on-year basis, production increased 1.2 per cent from 26,249 tonnes. Smallholders accounted for the bulk of NR production at 88.7 per cent, while estates contributed the remaining 11.3 per cent.
Malaysia's NR stocks also increased 5.2 per cent month-on-month to 129,524 tonnes in June from 123,149 tonnes in May.
Rubber processors held 77.8 per cent of total stocks, followed by rubber consumers at 22.1 per cent and rubber estates at 0.1 per cent.
NR exports rose 35.2 per cent month-on-month to 38,862 tonnes from 28,742 tonnes in May, with China remaining the largest destination, accounting for 55.8 per cent of total exports.
Germany followed at 11.5 per cent, the United States at 6.7 per cent, while Turkiye and India accounted for 3.1 per cent each.
Meanwhile, exports of rubber gloves, Malaysia's main rubber-based export product, increased 19.7 per cent month-on-month to RM1.4 billion in June from RM1.2 billion in May.
Average monthly rubber prices were mixed, with concentrated latex falling 3.6 per cent to 735.82 sen per kilogramme, while scrap rubber rose six per cent to 792.76 sen per kilogramme.
World Bank data showed that the price of Technically Specified Rubber 20 rose 1.8 per cent month-on-month to US$2.25 per kilogramme, while Singapore/Malaysia rubber increased 6.3 per cent to US$2.86 per kilogramme.
Despite the monthly recovery, Malaysia's NR production declined 8.1 per cent quarter-on-quarter to 65,266 tonnes in the second quarter of 2026 from 71,013 tonnes in the first quarter.
It was also down 4.7 per cent year-on-year from 68,513 tonnes in the second quarter of 2025.
The department said the Kuala Lumpur rubber market traded mixed in June, with prices initially supported by concerns over tightening supply in major producing countries amid severe El Nino conditions and prolonged dry weather.
Market sentiment was also supported by firm regional rubber futures, resilient economic activity in the US and China, stronger automotive demand and continued expansion of the global tyre industry.
However, prices retreated towards the end of the month following easing geopolitical tensions after the US-Iran ceasefire, which contributed to a sharp decline in crude oil prices and improved supply sentiment.

Title: Gamuda bags RM1.64bil solar, battery contracts in Australia
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Gamuda Bhd has clinched engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) contracts worth a combined A$569 million (RM1.64 billion) for two solar and battery hybrid projects in Queensland, Australia.
The construction firm said its Australian unit, DT Infrastructure Pty Ltd (DTI), had entered into the EPC contracts for the Ganymirra and Majors Creek projects.
DTI has received notices to proceed for both projects, which comprise two adjacent solar farms being developed as a single project. Each contract is valued at A$284.53 million, equivalent to about RM822.3 million.
Gamuda said the contracts are expected to commence in the second half of 2026, with a duration of two years and completion targeted for January 2029.
Under the contracts, DTI will undertake the design, procurement, construction, testing and commissioning of the solar farms, battery energy storage systems and associated balance-of-plant infrastructure.
Following completion, DTI will also provide operations and maintenance services for the assets to support their long-term performance, reliability and optimisation.
"The projects are expected to contribute positively to the revenue and earnings of the group for the financial year ending July 31, 2027, until the completion of the projects," Gamuda said in a bourse filing.
Once operational, the projects are expected to support Queensland's renewable energy transition by providing renewable power generation backed by large-scale battery storage.
The company said the projects would also help strengthen the state's electricity network and reduce carbon emissions.
Gamuda said DTI would also work with the Bindal People, the traditional custodians of the land on which the projects will be built, as well as local communities throughout the projects.
In a statement, DT Infrastructure chief executive officer John Anderson said the latest contract reflects the company's ability to safely deliver complex renewable energy projects.
"Projects like Ganymirra and Majors Creek are another demonstration of how renewable generation and large-scale battery storage are working together to deliver a more resilient and reliable electricity network," he said.
At peak construction the project is expected to support approximately 400 jobs in addition to opportunities for local businesses and suppliers, ensuring the economic benefits of the investment are shared across the Townsville region.
Edify Energy chief executive officer Ben Warne said the company had been impressed with DT Infrastructure's early execution of the Smoky Creek and Guthrie's Gap projects, as well as its partnership approach to delivery.
"We are looking forward to continuing the partnership with DT Infrastructure on these projects and to their safe and successful delivery," he said.

Title: Malaysia's labour demand grows 1.7pct to 9.25mil jobs in Q2
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's labour demand grew 1.7 per cent year-on-year to 9.25 million jobs in the second quarter of 2026 despite global uncertainties, the Statistics Department said.
The department said 97.9 per cent of the jobs were filled, while the remaining 2.1 per cent were vacancies.
Filled jobs rose 1.7 per cent to 9.05 million from 8.9 million a year earlier, led by the services sector, which grew 2.4 per cent and accounted for 53.4 per cent, or 4.83 million, of the total.
This was followed by the manufacturing sector with 2.42 million filled jobs and construction with 1.25 million.
By skills category, semi-skilled workers accounted for the largest share of filled jobs at 62.2 per cent, or 5.63 million, followed by skilled workers at 25.4 per cent and low-skilled workers at 12.4 per cent.
Job vacancies edged up 0.4 per cent year-on-year to 195,700, with the manufacturing sector accounting for the largest share at 114,000.
Meanwhile, 31,500 new jobs were created during the quarter, down 1.2 per cent from a year earlier, with the services sector accounting for 14,400 of the new positions.
"Overall, Malaysia's labour demand performance in Q2 2026 indicated that the national economy remained resilient, with the business sector continuing to absorb the labour force.
"This situation is proven by the growth in filled jobs and a low unemployment rate of 3.0 per cent," the department said.

Title: MN Holdings bags RM71mil TNB contract in Cameron Highlands
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: MN Holdings Bhd's subsidiary MN Power Transmission Sdn Bhd has secured a RM71.02 million contract from Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB) to establish a new 132/33 kilovolt (kV) transmission main intake (PMU) in Blue Valley, Cameron Highlands, Pahang.
In a bourse filing, the company said the contract involves the establishment of the new 132/33kV PMU Blue Valley, with a capacity of two 45 megavolt-amperes (MVA).
The works include the supply, erection, installation, testing and commissioning of the new PMU, featuring a double busbar arrangement, as well as the relevant primary and secondary systems and associated civil works.
MN Holdings said the contract took effect on Aug 12, 2026, with completion scheduled within 900 days from the commencement date.
Under the contract, MN Power Transmission is required to provide a performance security of RM3.551 million, equivalent to five per cent of the accepted contract value, within 56 days from the contract date.
The company expects the contract to contribute to future earnings and net assets per share upon commencement of the works.

Title: Poor response to subsidised health check scheme for commercial drivers - Loke
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The Transport Ministry's subsidised health screening programme for commercial vehicle drivers has received a poor response, with fewer than 20 drivers participating within a month of its launch.
Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook said the low uptake was disappointing, particularly as the programme was introduced to improve driver health and road safety while reducing the financial burden of medical examinations.
He said the programme, carried out in collaboration with the Social Security Organisation (Perkeso), allowed drivers to undergo the health screening for just RM30, with another RM55 subsidised by Perkeso.
"However, I am informed that until a few days ago, fewer than 20 drivers had participated in the scheme within a month of its launch, even though they only needed to pay RM30," he said.
Loke said many drivers continued to opt for the manual medical examination process, raising concerns over the ministry's ability to verify whether the existing approach was effectively improving drivers' health.
He said the ministry's digitally integrated approach was intended to make the health screening process more systematic and enable better monitoring.
"The manual method, we know, whether it really improves the driver's health or not, cannot be verified," he said in his speech at the ministry's monthly assembly here today.
Loke said the poor response highlighted the challenge of changing attitudes and mindsets among industry players towards safety initiatives.
He said such measures were not intended to burden drivers or the industry, but were aimed at improving safety and ensuring a healthier commercial transport sector.
"What we are doing is not to pressure anyone or add to their burden, but for safety and to ensure a healthier industry," he said.
Loke said driver health was one of the most fundamental aspects of road safety, as undetected medical conditions could increase risks not only to drivers but also other road users.
He said the ministry had introduced several initiatives to strengthen road safety, including vehicle telematics and the Health Check for Drivers programme, but launching an initiative alone was insufficient.
"What is important is that we look at its effectiveness and how we implement it," he said.
Loke said the ministry had launched numerous initiatives over the past several months but now needed to focus on ensuring they were properly implemented and achieved their intended outcomes.
"We cannot stop at simply launching initiatives. We must ensure every initiative we launch is effective and properly implemented," he said.
He said the issue would be among those discussed at the ministry's half-year strategic planning meeting scheduled for next week.
Launched on June 30, the Health Check for Drivers programme aims to enhance driver health through a reduced fee structure, with Perkeso covering RM55 of the RM85 cost across 500 participating clinics.
The initial phase is targeted to involve approximately 30,000 commercial drivers aged between 40 and 59.

Title: TH Act amendments being refined, consultations ongoing, says minister
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Proposed amendments to the Tabung Haji Act are being refined in consultation with various stakeholders, says Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan.
He said the changes will incorporate recommendations made by the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) into Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH).
Once approved by the cabinet, the proposed amendments will be tabled in Parliament.
"Presently, TH and various stakeholders are refining the amendments to provide the best possible framework for TH," he said after attending the Malaysian Islamic Dakwah Foundation Excellent Service Awards ceremony.
Zulkifli previously told the Dewan Rakyat
that the proposed amendments
would cover the regulatory framework for TH's fund management and investments.
Separately, Zulkifli described the decision by opposition members of parliament to walk out of the special parliamentary sitting on the RCI as irresponsible.
He said the report should have been debated collectively to allow MPs to raise questions, scrutinise the issues and work towards a solution.
He added that as the debate had concluded, authorities should be given space to manage investigations, enforce the law and take action.
The 211-page RCI report, published on July 29, examined the management and operations of TH between 2014 and 2020.
Among its key findings were weaknesses in governance, including political interference in management and profit distributions made without adequately accounting for impairment and declines in the fair value of investments.

Title: 25 companies seek financing under Penang climate mitigation fund
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: A total of 25 companies have expressed interest in securing financing under the Penang climate mitigation fund, with five currently undergoing the assessment process.
Chief minister Chow Kon Yeow said the fund, established under the Penang Green Industry Programme in partnership with Alliance Bank, has an initial allocation of RM20 million, comprising RM5 million from the state government and RM15 million from the bank, with a potential commitment of up to RM100 million.
"For a start, I've been informed that they are already processing some applications now. So that they can get the funding to carry out the necessary adaptation action plans in their respective factories," he told reporters after delivering his keynote address at the R.A.C.E To Zero: Penang Edition here today.
Also present were Infrastructure, Transport and Digital Committee chairman Zairil Khir Johari and Malaysian Photovoltaic and Sustainable Energy Industry Association president Justin Sim.
Earlier in his keynote address, Chow said eligible small and medium enterprises and mid-tier companies can access preferential financing of up to RM500,000, supported by grants, sustainability assessments and expert advisory services.
"Together with the Penang Green Council, the programme gives manufacturers a practical pathway to assess their sustainability needs and implement improvements," he said.
Chow said the shift towards clean energy is no longer simply an environmental concern but increasingly a competitiveness issue, particularly as global companies set stronger carbon targets across their supply chains.
He said this was particularly important for Penang, which recorded RM436.9 billion in electrical and electronics (E&E) exports last year, representing about 68 per cent of Malaysia's total E&E exports.
"Companies still look at talent, infrastructure, logistics, and cost. Increasingly, they are also asking, 'Where does your electricity come from?'
"Global companies are setting stronger carbon targets across their supply chains. They want access to renewable energy (RE) and lower Scope 2 emissions. For Penang's manufacturers, clean energy is no longer simply an environmental issue. It is a competitiveness issue," he said.
Chow said the Penang Energy Framework, launched in November 2024, targets a 25 per cent reduction in energy intensity and an increase in the share of RE in the state's energy mix to at least 10 per cent by 2030.
"Penang is land-scarce, so rooftop solar is one of our most practical solutions. Under our new building guidelines, new commercial and industrial buildings are expected to utilise at least 75 per cent of their roof area for solar panels or meet the relevant RE sourcing target according to their TNB tariff category," he said.
Chow said the state is also exploring other RE solutions, with the Penang Water Supply Corporation studying floating solar installations on its dams, while Silicon Island will incorporate RE into its development, including a Green Tech Park supported by solar generation.
He said energy efficiency is another important component of the transition, with the state introducing energy intensity standards to enable energy consumption to be measured, benchmarked and improved, while state government and local authority properties are being assessed for their RE and energy efficiency potential.
"For eligible new state government and local authority buildings, our target is for at least five per cent of total energy consumption to come from renewable sources, while existing government facilities are encouraged to work towards the same target," he said.
Chow said Penang's energy policies and programmes are also aligned with the federal government's National Energy Efficiency Action Plan 2.0, which targets an 11.6 per cent reduction in national energy demand by 2035, adding that federal and state efforts must move in the same direction towards cleaner energy, greater efficiency and stronger competitiveness.

Title: MACC's domestic probe into KWAP-eFishery investment nearly 80pct complete
Article:
KUCHING: The domestic component of the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission's (MACC) probe into KWAP's RM163.4 million investment in Indonesian aquaculture firm eFishery is nearly 80 per cent complete.
MACC chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said the international phase would take longer as investigators still require information and evidence from several foreign jurisdictions.
"To date, the domestic investigation has reached almost 80 per cent, while the investigation at the international level is still ongoing," he told a press conference here today.

Title: MACC completes probes into three TH RCI issues, submits recommendations
Article:
KUCHING: The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has completed investigations into three of the six original issues arising from the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Tabung Haji, with recommendations for charges and no further action (NFA) submitted.
MACC chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said investigations into the remaining three issues were also near completion.
"Of the six issues, three have been completed.
"There are recommendations for charges and there are recommendations for NFA.
"The other three are almost completed. We need to verify, analyse and finalise everything before announcing the status of the six issues," he told a press conference here today.
Abd Halim did not disclose which investigations resulted in recommendations for prosecution or NFA.

Title: Kelana Jaya LRT services return to normal after power outage
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Operations on the Kelana Jaya LRT line returned to normal at 10.25am today following an earlier power outage at the Universiti station.
Rapid KL, in a Facebook post, said the technical glitch, which occurred at 9.28am, left a train stranded between the Taman Jaya and Universiti stations.
The rail operator said alternative train services had been ended and passengers safely evacuated from the stranded train in accordance with its standard operating procedures.
"Passengers inside the affected train were safely transferred to a rescue train before being brought to a nearby station," Rapid KL said.
"The transfer process was closely monitored by operations staff to ensure passenger movement remained safe and controlled."
Rapid KL said affected commuters then continued their journeys on subsequent trains, with no injuries reported.
It said passenger transfers were a standard safety protocol designed to manage stranded train situations, particularly when technical or power failures prevented trains from moving forward.
"This procedure is carried out based on on-site assessments and is only executed once safety aspects are confirmed by the operating team.
"During the disruption, operations personnel activated temporary alternative train services to minimise the impact on commuters while technical teams were deployed to inspect and repair the affected power system."
Rapid KL said all repair and inspection works prioritised safety before full service was restored.
The affected train has been removed from service and sent for a thorough inspection to identify the root cause of the power failure.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MACC uncovers eight more investment issues in TH RCI probe
Article:
KUCHING: The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has uncovered eight additional investment-related issues in its probe linked to the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH).
MACC chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said the discoveries were separate from the six issues initially referred to the commission for investigation, bringing the total number of investigation papers opened to 14.
Halim told a press conference that the eight additional issues primarily involved investments and related decisions.
"The first involves Deru Semangat Sdn Bhd in relation to an oil palm plantation investment.
"The second concerns a property investment under Abraj Sdn Bhd."
The third involved construction and corporate investments related to Putrajaya Perdana Bhd, while the fourth concerned hotel investments in Mecca and Madinah under Al-Rawda Real Estate.
The fifth involved property investment in Saudi Arabia through the Alfareeda Residential Fund.
The remaining three involved property investment in Malaysia under TH Properties Sdn Bhd, support vessel services under Alam Maritim/TH Marine, and hotel and property investment in Malaysia under TH Hotel & Residences.
Halim said investigators would scrutinise agreements, contracts, meeting minutes and records relating to decisions made over the investments, adding that the extensive volume of documentation required specialised examination.
MACC has assigned six additional investigators to handle the new issues and could deploy more if necessary.
The commission is
also considering engaging external forensic experts
to assist in examining documents and other evidence.
Halim said discussions were ongoing at MACC's senior management level on engaging foreign expertise, including the costs involved.
Graft busters
began their probe into the RCI report on July 31
, following its declassification.
The RCI report, which covered the pilgrimage fund's management and operations between 2014 and 2020, identified governance weaknesses, including broad ministerial powers over appointments, overlapping roles among directors and senior management, and concerns over political influence.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Farage and Count Binface go head-to-head in snap UK poll
Article:
LONDON: Voters in eastern England head to the polls Thursday for a by-election triggered by hard-right Reform UK leader Nigel Farage, but amid a boycott by mainstream parties his main rival is a joke candidate called Count Binface.
The traditional parties have shunned the contest for the Clacton parliamentary seat – represented by Farage since July 2024 – denouncing his move to resign and launch a new vote as a stunt.
Polling stations open at 7 am (0600 GMT) with a total of 34 candidates in the running, forcing Farage to face off against dozens of fringe candidates, including Binface.
Brexit backer Farage – whose anti-immigration Reform UK won local elections in May and topped national polls for 18 months from early last year – has remained defiant.
He has framed the by-election as "the people of Clacton versus the Establishment", branding newspaper probes and official investigations into his finances and questionable donations to his anti-immigration party as a "stitch-up."
"Britain needs Reform, Britain wants Reform, and Britain demands a general election," he said in a statement late Wednesday.
Farage is widely expected to retain the eastern Essex seat, which voted overwhelmingly for Brexit in the 2016 referendum, and political analysts have downplayed the vote's wider significance.
"It seems unlikely that the by-election will be consequential for British politics," University of Southampton political science professor Will Jennings told AFP.
"Victory won't mean that questions about Farage or Reform's finances will go away, so it seems most likely it will be a wasted summer for everyone," he added.
[[nid:1510289]]
"When Farage returns to parliament afterwards we will be back where we started."
Polls will close at 10 pm, with counting beginning immediately and a result expected by around 7 am Friday.
Turnout – nearly 59 per cent in the 2024 general election – could be significantly down given the lack of traditional candidates from ruling centre-left Labour and the centre-right Conservatives.
Farage netted 46 per cent of the vote two years ago to become an MP on his eighth attempt, securing a majority of 8,405. But comparisons may be complicated by the boycotts.
Most of the candidates – the highest number of any parliamentary election – are standing as independents, and have led to a ballot paper which is nearly a metre long.
Joke candidate Count Binface, who dresses with a grey dustbin over his head wearing a cape and silver armour, has captured global media attention and could snatch a fifth of the votes, according to a Survation poll.
The self-styled "intergalactic space warrior" is part of a long British tradition of satirical election contenders, which appears to have reached its zenith in Clacton, where the Official Monster Raving Loony Party will also field three candidates.
"Farage's plan to turn this by-election into a serious political battle failed," Queen Mary University of London politics professor Stijn van Kessel told AFP, noting the resulting spectacle "makes Farage look rather silly."
Journalist Michael Crick, who wrote a 2022 biography of the Reform leader, agrees.
[[nid:1510288]]
"This has been a complete misjudgement by Farage," he told The Daily Telegraph. "He's hoping to become prime minister and Clacton is in no way representative of the country as a whole."
Farage shocked Westminster and beyond when he announced his resignation as Clacton MP – and intention to re-stand for the role – on July 7 following intense scrutiny of his and Reform's finances.
The parliamentary sleaze watchdog is investigating Farage and his deputy, Richard Tice, amid allegations they failed to declare financial gifts – including in Farage's case a £5 million (US$6.7 million) donation from cryptocurrency billionaire Christopher Harborne.
They deny any wrongdoing.
Meanwhile, London police have confirmed starting an investigation last year into donations to Reform before the 2024 general election.
UK media have reported it relates to non-declared financial support from longtime Farage ally and convicted fraudster George Cottrell and his mother.
The controversies have coincided with a drop in Reform polling support and in popularity for Farage, long a divisive figure loved and loathed in largely equal measure.
Luke Tryl, who heads the More in Common research non-profit, told AFP Farage's core supporters "seem largely undeterred" but that newer Reform converts "might now be wavering."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Khaled says navy personnel safe following training incident in South China Sea
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Royal Malaysian Navy (RMN) personnel were involved in an incident following a free-fall parachuting exercise in the South China Sea yesterday.
Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin confirmed the matter when contacted by the New Straits Times.
Khaled, however, did not indicate the nature of the incident nor the number of personnel involved.
"They were conducting a free-fall exercise. It did not involve any outside party," he said.
He said that the navy is expected to issue a press release on the incident.
The NST was made to understand that the personnel involved are all safe.
Sources said adverse weather had caused the personnel to drift from their intended landing area at one of the RMN's offshore naval stations in the South China Sea.
Harian Metro earlier reported that six members of the navy's Special Warfare Forces (Paskal) went missing after undergoing training as part of 'Eksesais Kerismas 29/26' at Pulau Layang-Layang last night.
The report said that a search and rescue (SAR) operation involving the vessels KD Teguh and KD Pahang found five personnel around 9pm.
Four were in stable condition while another sustained injuries believed to be from a shark attack.
The report said that all the personnel were brought to the Hospital Angkatan Tentera Wilayah Kota Kinabalu.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Power outage at Universiti station causes Kelana Jaya LRT delays
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Commuters on the Kelana Jaya LRT line faced morning delays after a power outage at the Universiti station left a train unable to operate.
Rapid KL confirmed the service disruption in a Facebook post, saying alternative train arrangements had been put in place to manage passenger flow.
Under the temporary service plan, trains operating from Putra Heights and Gombak were directed to turn back at the Asia Jaya station.
Rapid KL also announced temporary platform closures at several nearby stations to facilitate maintenance work.
Platform 2 at the Taman Bahagia and Taman Paramount stations was temporarily closed, while Platform 1 at the Taman Jaya station was similarly closed.
Commuters travelling through the affected areas were advised to adjust their boarding locations accordingly.
Passengers at Taman Bahagia and Taman Paramount stations were instructed to use Platform 1, while those at Taman Jaya station were required to board trains using Platform 2.
Passengers needing assistance or travel guidance were advised to approach station officers or Auxiliary Police personnel stationed at the affected stations.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Loke: Govt agencies needs to adapt communication strategies to reach younger Malaysians
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The Road Transport Department (RTD) has teamed up with Monsta Studios Sdn Bhd to deliver road safety messages through animation, creative content and digital communications, in a bid to better reach younger Malaysians.
Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook said the collaboration reflected the need for government agencies to adapt their communication strategies to reach their audiences.
He said conventional methods such as billboards, television advertisements and newspaper advertisements had their limitations, making creative digital content increasingly important.
"Today, everyone depends on smartphones. The explosion of information we see today revolves around social media and creative digital content.
"If we use our funds to put up big billboards, they still have their place, but they are less effective.
"Television advertisements are also less effective because not many people watch television anymore," he said at the Transport Ministry's monthly assembly and the National Month launching ceremony here today
Loke said government agencies needed to understand these changes and produce content that could convey messages quickly and effectively.
"Today, if something is more than one minute, people do not watch it. At best, 30 seconds or 20 seconds.
"Everything is instant now. This is a trend, not something we necessarily want or like, but it is the trend," he said.
He said the collaboration would combine RTD's expertise in road safety and regulations with Monsta's strengths in animation, creative content and digital communications.
This, he said, would help ensure road safety messages were not only understood but also internalised and practised by the public.
"This is another approach that we need to look at and develop further because our safety messages, or any message from the ministry in terms of communicating with the public, require greater creativity today.
"I hope this collaboration will become a catalyst for more collaborations between the public sector and the creative industry in delivering public-interest messages more effectively," he said.
Loke said the changing communications landscape presented a challenge not only to politicians but also to civil servants, who needed to understand how Malaysians consumed information today.
He added that government communication could no longer rely solely on traditional channels and agencies needed to adapt to current trends.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: DAP leadership engages northern delegates ahead of National Congress
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: About 400 DAP delegates from Penang, Kedah and Perlis attended an engagement session with party secretary-general Anthony Loke  and the Central Executive Committee (CEC) leadership here last night.
The session, held ahead of the party's national congress on Aug 16, served as a platform for delegates to exchange views on party affairs, national issues and the party's future direction.
Penang Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow, in a Facebook post today, said the session also aimed to strengthen unity among members before the congress in Putrajaya this Sunday.
"A heartfelt thank you to Loke, party leaders, delegates and comrades from the northern region for their participation and valuable insights," he said.
The upcoming congress is expected to see delegates deliberate on the party's position and future direction within the Unity Government.
The engagement session also follows a recent decision by the Perak DAP to remain in the Unity Government until the end of the current parliamentary term, citing the need for political stability and the continuation of reforms.
Perak DAP chairman Nga Kor Ming was previously reported as saying that remaining in the government would allow the party to continue contributing to policy-making while fulfilling its mandate to voters. BERNAMA

Title: Tun M backs F1 return to Sepang
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia should consider reclaiming its hosting rights for Formula 1 (F1) as changes in currency values have made hosting fees more manageable today, said former prime minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad.
Dr Mahathir said while rising costs forced the country to drop off the F1 calendar in 2017, the financial equation had since shifted.
"Money values have changed. In the past, RM100 million was huge, but today RM100 million feels like RM50 million used to," he said during the DR.M podcast.
"If I were in government, we would consider having our own race here again."
He was commenting on Sepang International Circuit (SIC) temporarily hosting the Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix. F1 and the Fédération Internationale de l'Automobile (FIA) recently confirmed that Malaysia will host the event from Oct 2 to 4.
Known for its 5.543km layout, sweeping high-speed corners and unpredictable tropical weather, the circuit remains one of F1's most recognisable venues.
Dr Mahathir urged the government to use the upcoming race as a benchmark to assess the economic returns of bringing back a permanent Malaysian Grand Prix.
Recalling the circuit's inception, Dr Mahathir said the decision to build Sepang on swampland in 1999 was a deliberate strategy to boost national tourism.
"When we started promoting tourism, people asked what we had since we didn't have pyramids like Egypt.
"We had to create events. F1 draws 100,000 spectators who stay in hotels, dine and spend money. It brings a massive inflow of foreign cash."
Dr Mahathir said the ultimate goal of hosting F1 in 1999 was never solely about ticket sales.
"Instead, it served as a global advertising mechanism that projected Malaysia's name into hundreds of millions of living rooms worldwide.
"The event put a developing nation on an equal footing with established European racing hubs, driving long-term destination awareness that benefited the retail, hospitality and airline sectors."
He said the original RM200 million construction cost of the circuit had long been fully recouped.
"We earned enough to cover the building cost, so we are essentially using the facility free of charge now. Whatever comes in now is profit."
Dr Mahathir said Malaysia gave up its hosting rights in 2017 after F1's American owners raised the annual hosting fees from RM50 million — backed by Petronas — to more than RM100 million.
"RM100 million was too high back then, and we couldn't afford it. But today, the returns on tourism and global exposure make it worth reconsidering."
He said Sepang held a distinct advantage over street tracks such as Singapore because it was purpose-built for high-speed racing without disrupting city traffic.

Title: Penang PH sticks to decision to accept BN, Umno
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Penang Pakatan Harapan remains committed to its decision to accept Barisan Nasional and Umno despite criticism from DAP adviser Lim Guan Eng.
Penang PH chairman Chow Kon Yeow said the decision was not questioned during a recent engagement session involving the state coalition.
"We stick to that decision," he said when asked about Penang PH's position.
Chow was responding to Lim's criticism of Penang PH's decision to accept BN and Umno, despite Lim describing statements by the two parties as unreasonable.
Chow said the matter was not raised by participants during the engagement session.
"That decision wasn't questioned. No one questioned it," he added.
Asked whether Lim was the only person to raise objections, Chow replied: "Just one person."
Chow's remarks reaffirmed Penang PH's position following its decision to work with BN and Umno at the state level.
Lim recently criticised Datuk Seri Reezal Merican Naina Merican's remarks on Umno-DAP ties in Penang, questioning whether Umno remained committed to maintaining trust within the state's unity government.
He described Reezal's comments
as "not just unfriendly but harsh" towards DAP and PKR, accusing him of unfairly claiming that the parties were engaging in identity politics.
Penang PH had recently
reaffirmed its electoral cooperation
with BN, saying the partnership remains important ahead of the next general election.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Loke: "Do I look nervous?...I am very relaxed"
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke said it was premature to speculate on his position as Transport Minister or the status of his party ahead of the DAP National Congress this Sunday.
Speaking to reporters here after a ministry function, Loke said he was "very relaxed" ahead of the party's National Congress. He dismissed questions that today's Transport Ministry assembly could be his last.
"How can you think this is my last press conference? I never said that. Let's talk after Sunday (the national congress)," he said at a press conference after attending the Transport Ministry's monthly assembly and the launch of its National Month celebrations here today.
The congress is expected to determine the party's direction, including whether it will remain in or withdraw from the federal government.
Loke will table a motion on the matter, which will be decided through a vote by 4,264 delegates from 1,704 eligible branches at the Putrajaya International Convention Centre (PICC).
Meanwhile, Loke also dismissed suggestions that he appeared nervous ahead of the congress, stressing that he remained calm.
"Do I look nervous? I don't know why you are asking such a question. I am very relaxed today," he said.

Title: Israel carries out first Gaza strike in more than week, one killed
Article:
GAZA CITY: Israel on Wednesday carried out its first air strike in more than a week in Gaza, both sides said, breaking a relative lull as the United States pressed a peace plan.
The Israeli military said it targeted a Hamas commander, charging that he had been planning attacks against Israeli forces operating in the war-battered territory.
"The fighter was struck in an aerial strike in order to remove the threat to IDF troops," a military statement said, adding that it tried to mitigate civilian harm.
Gaza's civil defence agency, a rescue service under Hamas, said the strike in Beit Lahia in the northern Gaza Strip targeted civilians riding in a tuk-tuk.
The strike killed Mohanad Saada, whose body was "torn to pieces", and wounded five other people, according to the civil defence agency and Al-Shifa Hospital.
A witness said Saada was among a group of workers who were repairing a wall damaged by Israeli shelling.
"It is true that Israeli airstrikes and assassinations had almost completely ceased for over a week, but today the occupation resumed its aerial bombardment," civil defence spokesman Mahmoud Bassal told AFP.
Israel had not carried out airstrikes in the Gaza Strip since August 3, following US President Donald Trump's announcement of a "major milestone" in his plan to end the war.
Hamas had announced that it would disarm by giving its weapons to a nascent Palestinian governing committee. Trump's "Board of Peace", in charge of implementing the ceasefire deal, had initially announced that Israel in turn would start a phased withdrawal from much of the Gaza Strip.
But Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Sunday publicly rejected the deal and vowed no Israeli pullout, even after the Board of Peace reassured him that Israel would not have to withdraw until complete Hamas disarmament.
Despite the statements by Netanyahu, who faces pushback from his right-wing base on Gaza ahead of tight elections in October, Israel had been seen as largely complying with the Trump plan by avoiding major strikes.
The two sides agreed to a ceasefire pushed by Trump in October, after which Israel reduced but did not end military operations.
Israeli operations in Gaza have killed 1,259 Palestinians since the ceasefire, according to the territory's health ministry, which operates under Hamas authority and whose figures are considered reliable by the United Nations.
The Israeli army has reported five deaths in its ranks during the same period.--AFP

Title: VSTECS shares rise 3.42pct in early trade after firmer Q2 results
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: VSTECS Bhd's share price rose 3.42 per cent in early trade today after the company announced its net profit for the second quarter of 2026.
At 10.17am, its shares gained six sen to RM1.81 with 5.23 million shares traded.
The information technology provider posted a 50 per cent increase in net profit to RM30.31 million from RM20.17 million in the same period a year ago, driven by growth across all business segments.
In a Bursa Malaysia filing yesterday, it said the revenue jumped 31.7 per cent to RM1.08 billion from RM818.87 million previously.
The performance was driven by higher sales across all three business segments -- information and communications technology (ICT) distribution, enterprise systems, and ICT services.

Title: Thai mother's RM1,500 journey back to work in Johor ends in arrest
Article:
TUMPAT: A Thai mother's attempt to return to her workplace in Malaysia after spending time with her children in Pattani ended with her arrest for illegal entry yesterday.
The 24-year-old woman, who only wanted to be known as Nadia, had paid RM1,500 to an agent to arrange her journey back to a restaurant in Pasir Gudang, Johor, where she had worked for the past two years.
However, her journey ended when she was detained by a General Operations Force (GOF) task force from the Seventh Battalion in Tanah Merah for entering Malaysia without valid travel documents.
Nadia said she had returned to her hometown in Pattani last month to care for her children after her two-year-old twins fell ill.
She said she later decided to return to Malaysia to resume work and earn a living for her three children.
"Since divorcing my husband in 2023, I have been raising my children, aged six and two-year-old twins, on my own.
"To feed my children, I have to work in Malaysia and have been using the services of the agent since 2024," she said when interviewed yesterday.
Nadia said she was aware of the risks of entering Malaysia without valid travel documents but felt she had little choice as she needed to return to work.
"I know that both the Thai and Malaysian governments encourage people to use legal routes when entering and leaving the countries.
"But I was stubborn and did not apply for a valid travel document. This is my fault, and I now have to face the consequences," she said.
Nadia said she hoped her children would be taken care of while she dealt with the legal proceedings.
She is being investigated under Section 6(1) of the Immigration Act 1959/63 for illegal entry.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: South Korean shares hit 3-week high as chipmakers jump
Article:
SEOUL: South Korean shares rose on Thursday to hit their highest levels in three weeks, led by a jump in chipmakers, tracking overnight gains in US AI and semiconductor stocks.
The benchmark KOSPI was up 245.50 points, or 3.73 per cent, at 6,824.54 as of 0138 GMT, hitting its highest level since July 24.
Shares of chipmakers SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics rallied more than 7 per cent and 5 per cent, respectively. A report that Singapore state investor Temasek plans to invest in the memory chipmakers also buoyed sentiment around the semiconductor sector.
The S&P 500 and the Nasdaq ended higher on Wednesday, lifted by upbeat quarterly results from CoreWeave and other AI infrastructure firms, while mild inflation data reinforced bets that the US Federal Reserve will hold interest rates steady in September.
Among other South Korean index heavyweights, battery maker LG Energy Solution climbed 1.95 per cent, while Hyundai Motor and sister automaker Kia Corp were up 2.93 per cent and up 1.62 per cent, respectively.
Steelmaker POSCO Holdings shed 0.08 per cent, while drugmaker Samsung BioLogics rose 0.84 per cent.
Of the total 900 traded issues, 397 shares advanced, while 453 declined.
Foreigners were net buyers of shares worth 1.1 trillion won (US$778.53 million).
The won was quoted at 1,413.1 per dollar on the onshore settlement platform, 0.38 per cent higher than its previous close at 1,418.5.
In money and debt markets, September futures on three-year treasury bonds gained 0.04 point to 103.35. The most liquid three-year Korean treasury bond yield fell by 0.2 basis point to 3.778 per cent, while the benchmark 10-year yield rose by 0.2 basis point to 4.293 per cent.

Title: South Korea unveils package to boost housing supply, support young buyers
Article:
SEOUL: South Korea said on Thursday it would raise financial support for construction projects and ease regulations for young homebuyers as part of efforts to stabilise a red-hot housing market.
Earlier this month, the government of President Lee Jae Myung proposed higher taxes on wealthy homeowners. Lee's approval ratings have been falling on rising house prices and stock market volatility.
Thursday's measures are aimed at "stabilising the property market by stimulating housing supply and through a comprehensive financial package for young people and those with actual demand," the Financial Services Commission said in a statement.
The FSC said it would raise policy support for financing construction projects to 47.8 trillion won (US$33.72 billion) or more, from a planned 26.3 trillion won, to boost housing supply.
The FSC also announced financial support measures, such as new policy loans, for young people and newlyweds who buy a house to live in, while maintaining or tightening restrictions on speculative demand.
South Korea, one of the world's most indebted countries, has complex borrowing rules in place in a bid to curb household debt. The FSC said it would manage debt growth at around 3 per cent this year, up from the previous target of 1.5 per cent.
President Lee's approval ratings hit a one-month low of 51 per cent in a survey by Gallup Korea on July 24, with housing market policy being cited as one of the main factors, after house prices rose in June by the most since November 2021.

Title: [UPDATED] Soldier injured in Port Dickson firing range mishap
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A soldier was injured in a shooting mishap at a firing range in Port Dickson during a live-fire drill.
The Army Strategic Communication Branch said the incident occurred at 2.15pm yesterday at the firing range in Menyala, Port Dickson, while soldiers were undergoing training for the Malaysian Army Shooting Skills Test (UKMTD) competition.
"The other soldier was conducting dry-fire training and fired at a target from a distance of 25m, unaware that Trooper Muhammad Akhmal Shahrudin was still behind the target.
"He sustained an injury to his right cheek, with the bullet passing through his left lower jaw," it said in a statement.
Akhmal was rushed to Port Dickson Hospital for initial treatment.
A medical examination found no internal injuries, while his condition was reported to be stable. He was sedated for further treatment.
The Army said it would conduct a detailed investigation to determine the cause and factors that led to the incident.
"An internal investigation will also be conducted," it said.
Earlier, Negri Sembilan deputy police chief Senior Assistant Commissioner Nasharudin Mohd Shariff said police had received a report on the incident.
He said preliminary investigations found that the victim was at the firing range with several other soldiers when he was hit by a round fired by a fellow serviceman.
"The victim sustained facial injuries and was taken to Port Dickson Hospital for initial treatment before being referred to Tuanku Ja'afar Hospital, Seremban.
"He is reported to be in stable condition," he said in a statement.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Oil drops on lower demand forecasts despite deadlock in US-Iran talks
Article:
BEIJING: Oil prices fell more than US$1 on Thursday as forecasters lowered global oil demand projections for 2026 because of the disruptions from the US-Israeli war on Iran, though the supply constraints from the conflict provided a floor for the market.
Brent futures dropped US$1.29, or 1.5 per cent, at US$87.69 a barrel by 0100 GMT. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude fell US$1.30, or 1.6 per cent, to US$81.97.
The Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries lowered its world oil demand growth forecast for 2026 to 580,000 barrels per day in its monthly oil market report on Wednesday.
On the same day, the International Energy Agency said it expects a 1.6 million bpd contraction in consumption this year, down from a forecast of 1 million bpd last month, because of restricted fuel supplies and higher prices from the US-Israeli war on Iran that have curtailed demand.
Oil prices were also under pressure from a surprise build in US commercial crude oil inventories, which posted their largest weekly gain since January 2023 last week as exports slumped, the Energy Information Administration said on Wednesday.
Crude inventories rose by 17.4 million barrels to 424.4 million barrels in the week ended August 7, their highest since June 5, the EIA said, compared with analysts' expectations in a Reuters poll for a 1.4 million-barrel draw.
Still, the deadlocked talks between Iran and the US to end the war in the Gulf have kept prices elevated.
A senior Iranian source said on Wednesday that there had been no progress in talks to revive the interim deal agreed in June and define a time frame to implement it.
Attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz and the Bab el-Mandeb Strait on Tuesday, two crucial export routes for Middle Eastern oil and gas, highlight the risks that remain for crude supply from the region.
"The safety situation for navigation in these waters has further deteriorated, forcing vessels to turn off their signals, which reduces transparency in shipping and makes it more difficult for the market to track and assess actual supply levels," analysts at Haitong Futures said in a note.

Title: Yuan at 3-1/2-year high as US inflation dims Fed rate hike prospects
Article:
SHANGHAI: China's yuan firms to a 3-1/2-year high against the dollar on Thursday, as US inflation data weighed on the greenback and dimmed prospects for an imminent Federal Reserve rate hike.
US consumer prices were in line with expectations, easing appreciation pressure on the dollar in the near term and lending the yuan a broadly steady to slightly firmer bias, market participants said.
The spot yuan opened at 6.7455 per dollar and was last trading at 6.7441 as of 0251 GMT, 18 pips firmer than the previous late session close. It hit 6.74 per dollar in early trade, the strongest since February 2023.
"Two muted inflation prints in a row should be sufficient to quell worries that price pressures are broadening beyond energy," DBS analysts said in a note, adding that a cooling labour market removed the case for near-term Fed tightening.
The greenback's upside was also capped by the worst US budget deficit since March 2021, they said. Prior to the market opening, the People's Bank of China set the midpoint rate at 6.7888 per dollar, 418 pips weaker than a Reuters' estimate.
The spot yuan is allowed to trade a maximum of 2 per cent on either side of the fixed midpoint each day. The central bank has been gradually strengthening its daily yuan guidance but at levels weaker than market expectations, suggesting it wants to manage the pace of appreciation.
UBS analysts said seasonal factors could come into play as September approaches, with typically strong autumn export flows potentially lending support to the offshore yuan.
However, the magnitude of any such appreciation would likely hinge on the PBOC midpoint fixing strategy, they said. The yuan is up 0.6 per cent against the dollar this month, and 3.7 per cent firmer this year.
The offshore yuan traded at 6.745 per dollar, up about 0.01 per cent in Asian trade. The dollar index, which measures the greenback against a basket of currencies including the yen and the euro, was steady at 100.
The PBOC said on Wednesday that it would conduct up to 600 billion yuan (US$88.98 billion) worth of overnight reverse repos per day on August 14 and August 17-19. The central bank uses the short-term liquidity tool to fine-tune cash conditions in the country's banking system.

Title: Venezuela govt, opposition wrap up round of post-Maduro talks
Article:
CARACAS: Venezuela's interim government and opposition representatives on Wednesday wrapped up a first round of talks aimed at reconciling the nation following the US ouster of longtime leader Nicolas Maduro.
A joint statement issued by the two sides highlighted agreement on two topics after several days of discussion: reforming the judiciary, and seeking access to frozen funds to aid in earthquake recovery efforts.
Both sides committed to "initiate a process that contributes to the transformation of the justice system," including "Reforms to the Organic Law" of Venezuela's top court, the Supreme Tribunal of Justice (TSJ).
The TSJ notably validated Maduro's 2024 reelection, despite serious allegations of fraud and no public release of the official results.
The document did not mention the National Electoral Council, another body the opposition hopes to overhaul after it also upheld Maduro's disputed victory.
In light of the devastating twin earthquakes on June 24, which have left over 6,300 people dead, both sides also agreed to work toward the release "Venezuela's international reserve assets held at the Bank of England."
Under Maduro, Venezuela had tried repeatedly and unsuccessfully to access the funds.
The joint statement also called for the establishment of "mechanisms for transparency, traceability, and auditing" to make sure the funds are properly used.
Interim president Delcy Rodriguez's government was represented at the talks by her brother Jorge Rodriguez, who is also the head of Venezuela's National Assembly.
Delcy Rodriguez was Maduro's vice president, but has nonetheless led the country with Washington's blessing, and has won praise from US President Donald Trump for acceeding to his administration's desires.
- 'NO NAIVETE' -
The opposition was meanwhile represented by Dinorah Figuera, leader of the political bloc that won a majority in the 2015 National Assembly, the last legislature elected in a vote widely recognized by the international community.
Notably absent from the table is exiled opposition leader and Nobel Peace Prize laureate Maria Corina Machado, who has said she will not stand in the way of the process.
Many Venezuelans are hopeful that the transition talks will lead to democratic elections.
Over the last six days of talks, Figuera met separately with representatives of political prisoners, retirees and media workers and promised to advocate for their demands.
"We are in this process to achieve a democratic and free Venezuela," the politician wrote on X on Tuesday.
Dozens of opposition supporters gathered outside the hotel in Caracas where the talks were being held.
A source from the opposition delegation, who requested anonymity, compared the interim government to Nicaragua's oppressive administration, which the United States considers a dictatorship.
"There is no naivete on the part of the opposition delegation," the source said, adding that it "must take advantage of this window of opportunity."
Elections will only be announced after the reforms give way to a new Electoral Council, the source believes, adding that laws regulating terrorism and dissent need reforms due to their past use to persecute political prisoners.
The source told AFP the delegation viewed Machado as "the leader of the Venezuelan opposition...she is the voice that Venezuelans identify as their own."
Some commentators believe that US President Donald Trump has vetoed Machado's return to Venezuela, which Washington denies.
The US leader has repeatedly voiced satisfaction with Rodriguez's administration.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Illegals busted running gambling outlet under guise of grocery shop
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Immigration Department has busted an illegal gambling operation disguised as a grocery shop in Taman Serdang Perdana, Seri Kembangan.
The premise was allegedly used as a front to conceal the gambling operation and had been operating for about four months, from 9am until 3am the following day.
Immigration officers who got wind of the gambling den raided the place yesterday and detained six individuals, including a woman believed to be the caretaker, three Bangladeshi men and two Indonesian women, aged between 20 and 45.
The operation began at 3pm and followed a month-long intelligence operation based on public information and surveillance.
Initial checks showed that the caretaker had overstayed, while the other five foreigners did not possess valid passes or travel documents to remain in the country.
The detainees were taken to the Putrajaya Immigration Office for further action.
The raiding team also seized eight tablets, an Indonesian passport, a Travel Document in Lieu of a Passport issued by the Indonesian government, a copy of the business licence and gambling vouchers.
Meanwhile, two men, including a Pakistani national, have been issued with notices to appear at the department to assist investigations.
