Title: Alam Flora regrets impact, pledges safety focus as Pantai Hillpark lorry crash probe continues
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 13 — Alam Flora has pledged its full cooperation with authorities in the probe into a crash involving one of its compactor garbage lorries along Jalan Pantai Murni 1, Pantai Hillpark, yesterday.
In a statement today, Alam Flora informed that the vehicle will be sent for inspection to identify the exact cause of the incident, in line with instructions from the investigating officer.
The company emphasised that the safety and well-being of its workers, contractorsand the public remain its top priority.
“This matter is being treated with the utmost seriousness, and any necessary follow-up actions will be taken based on the investigation’s findings.
“We deeply regret the impact this incident has had on the affected community and remain committed to ensuring high safety standards in all our operational activities,” the statement read.
In the early-morning incident yesterday, a garbage lorry is believed to have experienced a brake failure before losing control and crashing into the perimeter wall of a condominium.
The lorry driver has lodged a report withthe Kuala Lumpur Traffic Police Station, and a breathalyser by the police confirmed that he was not under the influence of alcohol.
The compactor lorry will be sent to the Computerised Vehicle Inspection Centre (Puspakom) for examination, and the case is being investigated under Section 43(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987. — Bernama

Title: Perak police probe sexual harassment allegations against PKNPk CEO
Article:
IPOH, Aug 13 — Perak police have opened an investigation into alleged slander involving sexual harassment claims against Perak State Development Corporation (PKNPk) chief executive officer Datuk Redza Rafiq Abdul Razak, following a report lodged by the corporation.
State police chief commissioner Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said the investigation was initiated based on the police report lodged by PKNPk over the matter, which had been circulated on social media.
“Police have opened an investigation under Section 507A of the Penal Code and Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998.
“The investigation is still ongoing,” he told a press conference at the Perak Police Headquarters here.
Mohd Alwi said police had yet to receive any report from the alleged sexual harassment victim.
He also said police were also awaiting a response from the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) regarding the TikTok account linked to the allegations.
“Further investigations would be conducted once police received the information from MCMC,” he added.
Mohd Alwi also said no witnesses had been called to have their statements recorded so far, as police were still trying to identify the owner of the TikTok account.
Yesterday, PKNPk, in a statement, said reports were lodged with the police and MCMC over the dissemination of various allegations against the corporation, its management and certain individuals linked to the organisation.
PKNPk said it was aware of several posts by a Facebook page that had recently been publishing various serious allegations against PKNPk and its management.

Title: Meth, heroin and cannabis worth RM18,500 found inside a Lumut police cell, and a cop's in trouble too
Article:
IPOH, Aug 13 — Three men, including a police constable, were arrested after police seized drugs worth RM18,534 at the Lumut police station lock-up in Manjung.
Perak police chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said the drugs were found during an inspection of the lock-up on Tuesday at about 8.30am.
He said police found 16 small plastic tubes containing 109g of methamphetamine, 16 plastic tubes containing 110g of heroin and 23 tubes containing 142g of dried cannabis leaves.
“Following the seizure, we arrested two suspects, in their 40s, who are supposed to be charged for drugs-related offences.
“We also arrested the policeman, in his 30s, who is stationed at the location, to assist the investigation,” he said at a press conference at the Perak police headquarters here.
He said the two drug suspects tested positive for drugs, while all three individuals have been remanded for seven days from August 12 to 18.
Mohd Alwi said police are also investigating how the drugs were smuggled into the lock-up.
He said police take drug abuse and trafficking seriously, including cases involving individuals within police premises or surrounding areas, and would conduct a transparent and thorough investigation to determine appropriate action based on the evidence.
The case is being investigated under Section 39B and Section 15(1)(a) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952.
If convicted under Section 39B, offenders face the death penalty or life imprisonment and whipping of at least 12 strokes, while those convicted under Section 15(1)(a) face a fine of up to RM5,000, imprisonment for up to two years, or both.

Title: Transport minister urges commercial vehicle drivers to make RM30 health screening count as fewer than 20 sign up
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 13 — Fewer than 20 commercial vehicle drivers have taken up the government’s subsidised health screening programme since it was launched last month, Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook said today.
Loke said the response to the Pemandu Sihat dan Selamat (PSS) initiative remained low despite eligible drivers having to pay only RM30 for a comprehensive health examination, with the Social Security Organisation (Socso) subsidising the remaining RM55.
“I was informed a few days ago that not even 20 people had participated within the one-month period that we had planned,” he said in his speech at the Transport Ministry’s monthly assembly and launch of its National Month celebrations here.
The initiative, launched on June 30 and implemented from July 1, targets about 30,000 commercial vehicle drivers aged between 40 and 59 in its initial phase.
Loke said the programme was aimed at improving the health and wellbeing of drivers, particularly those responsible for carrying passengers and operating commercial vehicles.
“When we look after the welfare of drivers, we are actually looking after the safety of road users,” he said.
Speaking to reporters later, Loke said the low participation could be because the programme was still new and greater awareness was needed among drivers.
He said the government had deliberately reduced the cost of the health screening to RM30 through the Socso subsidy, but drivers had yet to take advantage of the initiative.
“It is a good programme that offers subsidies and we have reduced the cost to only RM30 for drivers to pay, but not many have taken the initiative or responded to it,” he said.
Loke urged drivers, particularly older ones, to undergo comprehensive health screenings to identify potential health problems early.
He said conditions such as high blood pressure and diabetes could go undetected if drivers did not undergo proper medical examinations.
Loke said the initiative was also aimed at addressing shortcomings in the existing health certification process for commercial drivers.
While health examinations have long been mandatory, drivers previously only had to submit a medical examination form certified by a doctor or clinic when renewing their vocational licences.
He said this made it difficult to determine whether a thorough physical examination had actually been carried out or not.
“We are not saying it was not done, but it simply could not be determined whether a thorough examination had been conducted,” he said.
Under the new system, doctors at participating clinics will key in their findings directly into an online system, which will then be integrated with JPJ’s MySikap platform.
This means drivers’ health reports will be available when they renew their licences, eliminating reliance on physical forms.
The programme was launched in collaboration with the Human Resources Ministry, Socso, JPJ and the Malaysian Medical Association.
The initial phase involves 500 participating clinics and is scheduled to run from July to December.
The government has allocated RM12.4 million for the programme, including RM7 million from Socso and RM5.4 million from the Finance Ministry.
Loke said the government hoped more drivers would take advantage of the programme and undergo proper health checks rather than simply having forms certified.
“Usually, drivers will just take the form to be certified by doctors. We hope to change that so that they undergo a thorough check-up and find out whether they have any health conditions,” he said.

Title: ‘I am very relaxed’: Loke dismisses talk of final ministry assembly before DAP congress decision
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 13 — Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook today played down suggestions that this could be his last monthly assembly with Transport Ministry staff ahead of DAP’s crucial vote on Sunday on whether the party should remain in the federal government.
Asked whether today’s ministry assembly could be his final one with ministry staff, Loke dismissed the assumption.
“How do you think it is my last? I have never mentioned that,” he told reporters after the Transport Ministry’s monthly assembly here today.
Asked if he was nervous ahead of the DAP special congress on Sunday, Loke said he was relaxed.
“I don’t know why you ask such a question. I am very relaxed today. I am celebrating with my secretary-general for his birthday. So, after this, we have a birthday celebration for him. Thank you very much,” he said.
Loke’s remarks came three days before DAP delegates are due to vote on a motion that could determine whether the party’s leaders, including its Cabinet members, remain in the government for the rest of the current parliamentary term.
The secret ballot will be held at DAP’s national congress on Sunday, with roughly 4,000 delegates expected to take part. The motion concerns DAP’s participation in the federal government and does not involve the party’s position in Pakatan Harapan.
The vote follows a string of electoral setbacks for DAP and PH, including the party’s loss of all eight seats it contested in the Sabah election last November, followed by further defeats in Johor and Negeri Sembilan.
Loke was among the casualties in the latest setback, losing his Chennah state seat after three terms.
Despite the electoral losses, Loke has previously said the decision on whether DAP should remain in government will be left to the delegates.
DAP currently holds five ministerial positions and seven deputy minister posts in the federal administration.
The party has said that even if delegates vote for its leaders to relinquish their government positions, DAP would continue supporting Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim in Parliament until the end of the current term.
For now, however, Loke appears content to wait until Sunday before discussing what comes next.
“After Sunday, we talk,” he said.

Title: Jobstreet: Firms still keen on hiring, job ads grew 33pc year-on-year
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 13 — Jobstreet said the Malaysian job market appeared resilient in the face of a global supply crisis, as firms continue to show keenness in hiring despite the slight increase in the official unemployment rate.
Job ads on its platform increased by 33 per cent year-on-year as employers appear to be actively looking for talent across the market, Southeast Asia’s largest online employment and career recruitment platform said in a statement today, in line with the Department of Statistics Malaysia’s data that suggests Malaysia’s labour market remains broadly resilient.
“Jobstreet’s platform data reflects continued hiring demand. In H1 2026, job ads increased by 33 per cent year-on-year, showing that employers are still actively looking for talent across the market,” said Nicholas Lam, managing director, Jobstreet by SEEK Malaysia.
Demand remains broad.
Manufacturing, transport and logistics accounted for the largest share of job ads at 12 per cent, followed by accounting at 11 per cent, sales at 10 per cent, engineering at 9 per cent, and administration and office support at 8 per cent, the platform said citing its internal data.
At the same time, DOSM reported that skill-related underemployment remained at 35.2 per cent.
Lim said this points to an ongoing skills-matching challenge: jobs are available, but workers may not always have the right skills for where demand is growing.
“For jobseekers, this makes it increasingly important to understand where opportunities are, build relevant and transferable skills, and position their experience towards areas of demand,” he said.
“For employers, clearer skills requirements and looking beyond traditional qualifications can help widen the available talent pool.”
The labour force expanded by 0.3 per cent in the second quarter of 2026, increasing by 43.7 thousand persons to 17.28 million persons, up from 17.23 million persons in the January to March period, DOSM said.
The Labour Force Participation Rate remained unchanged at 70.9 per cent, the same rate recorded in the preceding quarter.

Title: Kelana Jaya LRT services fully restored after power outage near University station
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 13 — Kelana Jaya LRT services returned to normal at 10.25am today after a power supply disruption at Universiti station left a train stranded between Taman Jaya and Universiti stations, Rapid KL said.
The rail operator said the disruption began at about 9.28am, prompting passengers on the affected train to be transferred to a rescue train under established safety procedures.
“Passengers on the train were safely transferred to a rescue train at the location before being taken to a nearby station,” it said.
Rapid KL said the passengers subsequently continued their journeys on another train, with no injuries reported.
It said transferring passengers between trains is an established safety procedure when a train is stranded and unable to continue because of a technical fault or power disruption.
“This procedure was carried out based on an assessment of conditions at the location and only after safety aspects had been confirmed by the responsible operations team,” it said.
Alternative train services were also activated temporarily to reduce the impact of the disruption on commuters.
Rapid KL said its technical team was deployed to inspect and restore the affected system, with safety checks carried out before normal operations resumed.
“The train involved has been taken out of service and sent to the depot for further inspection and investigation to determine the actual cause of the incident,” it said.
Rapid KL apologised for the inconvenience and thanked passengers for their patience and cooperation throughout the disruption.

Title: Passenger falls onto tracks at Gombak LRT station, causing brief Kelana Jaya Line disruption, says Rapid KL
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 13 — Explaining a brief disruption to Kelana Jaya LRT services this morning, Rapid KL said a passenger believed to have fainted fell onto the tracks at Gombak station at about 9.05am.
The rail operator said the incident prompted the station’s Platform Intrusion Emergency Stop (PIES) system to be activated and power to the tracks to be temporarily cut.
“Immediately after the incident, the Platform Intrusion Emergency Stop (PIES) system was activated and power supply to the tracks was temporarily cut off as a safety measure to allow the operations team and auxiliary police to take immediate action,” it said in a statement.
Operations personnel and auxiliary police helped the passenger out of the track area and took them to the station’s emergency room while waiting for an ambulance.
Rapid KL said the passenger was subsequently taken to Tawakal Hospital Kuala Lumpur for further examination and treatment.
It said a subsequent inspection confirmed that the tracks were safe for use, with train operations resuming at 9.12am, about seven minutes after the incident.

Title: Penang Pakatan sticking with BN, Umno despite criticism, says Chow Kon Yeow
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Aug 13 — Penang Pakatan Harapan (PH) is sticking with its decision to continue working with Barisan Nasional (BN), including Umno, despite criticism from DAP adviser Lim Guan Eng, state PH chairman Chow Kon Yeow said today.
Chow said the decision remained Penang PH’s position and was not challenged during a state DAP internal engagement session held yesterday.
“We are sticking with that decision. The decision was not questioned yesterday; no one questioned it,” he told reporters after officiating the R.A.C.E to Zero Penang edition event here.
Chow, who is also Penang chief minister, was responding to questions over the state DAP leadership’s continued cooperation with BN and Umno.
He said he was unsure whether objections to the decision had been raised by only one person or more outside the meeting.
Lim had previously questioned Penang PH’s decision to continue its cooperation with BN and Umno in the state administration, despite what he described as unfriendly attacks against DAP and PKR.
The former Penang chief minister said the position was difficult to understand when there had been no response to remarks by Bertam assemblyman Datuk Seri Reezal Merican Naina Merican, whom he accused of making baseless allegations against DAP and PKR over identity politics.
Reezal had denied that BN exploited identity politics during the recent Negeri Sembilan state election and instead accused DAP and PKR of focusing on one ethnic group, according to Lim.
Penang PH had on Saturday decided to maintain its cooperation with BN and Umno in the state administration, including retaining BN’s sole state executive councillor Datuk Rashidi Zinol.
Chow also confirmed that DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke attended the party’s internal engagement session in Penang yesterday.
Loke has been meeting DAP members in several states ahead of the party’s national congress, where delegates are expected to deliberate on the party’s continued participation in the federal unity government.

Title: JPJ taps BoBoiBoy, PapaZola to help push road safety campaigns to Gen Z and younger audiences
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 13 — The Road Transport Department (JPJ) is teaming up with local animation studio Monsta Studios to bring road safety messages to younger Malaysians through animation and digital content.
Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook said the collaboration was part of efforts to strengthen the country’s road safety agenda by using digital content, animation, social media and creative storytelling to deliver safety messages.
“In our efforts to foster a culture of safety, our approach must also evolve in line with changing times. Young people today are more engaged with digital content, animation, social media and creative storytelling,” he said in his speech at the Transport Ministry’s monthly assembly and launch of its National Month celebrations today.
“Therefore, road safety messages must also be delivered through mediums that are close to them, more creatively, in ways that are easy to understand and easy to remember.
“The collaboration between JPJ and Monsta Studios, which combines JPJ’s expertise in road safety and road regulations with Monsta Studios’ strengths in animation, creative content and digital communication, will ensure that road safety messages are understood, embraced and ultimately practised by the public,” he added
Loke said traditional advertising methods such as billboards, television and newspapers were becoming less effective amid declining viewership and readership, making digital content increasingly important in reaching younger audiences.
He said video content had become the language of younger generations, particularly Gen Z, whose media consumption habits differed from those of previous generations.
At a press conference later, Loke said the initiative was also aimed at reaching schoolchildren.
Monsta Studios is the Malaysian animation studio behind popular franchises such as BoBoiBoy and Mechamato, as well as
Papa Zola The Movie
.
Loke also thanked Monsta Studios for its willingness to establish the strategic collaboration with JPJ and the Transport Ministry, saying the partnership could pave the way for further cooperation between the public sector and creative industry.
“I hope this collaboration will serve as a catalyst for more partnerships between the public sector and the creative industry in delivering messages of public interest more effectively,” he said.

Title: Penang may advise schools to suspend outdoor activities if air quality worsens, says CM
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Aug 13 — The Penang government may advise schools to suspend or postpone outdoor activities if air quality in the state worsens, Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow said today.
He said Air Pollutant Index (API) readings in Penang remained at moderate levels for now, but the state government was closely monitoring the situation.
“Any further action will depend on the API readings and how the current situation develops.
“At the moment, the readings are still moderate. If they reach more critical levels, I think advice will have to be issued to halt or postpone certain activities,” he told reporters after officiating the R.A.C.E to Zero Penang edition event here.
Chow was responding to questions over Penang’s API readings, which had approached the 100 mark earlier this morning.
He said postponing outdoor activities at schools was among the measures that could be considered should air pollution worsen.
“Some schools may have to postpone outdoor activities and so on. We will deal with that when it reaches that level,” he said.
Chow said the state government was receiving updates from the state secretary and the Department of Environment (DoE) on air quality conditions.
“I will issue a statement later. It is too complex for me to explain now.
“So, we have asked our office to issue a statement regarding the API readings in Penang,” he said.
As of 9am today, air quality in 11 areas across the country was at unhealthy levels, with Sarawak recording the most affected areas, according to the Malaysian Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS).
Hot weather across the region since last week have contributed to forest fires in Indonesia, where more than 107,000 hectares have reportedly been affected so far, about twice the area previously recorded.

Title: Medan Pasar set for climate-resilient revamp under KL ‘sponge city’ push, says Hannah Yeoh
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 13 — Historic Medan Pasar in downtown Kuala Lumpur is set for a revamp aimed at improving rainwater management and public accessibility while preserving its heritage identity, Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh said today.
In a Facebook post, Yeoh said the project is a collaboration between Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) and Yayasan Creador, with the public space to be made more open, accessible and welcoming to the community.
“This project embraces Nature-based Solutions, with improved rainwater management.”
“It is part of our wider effort to build a more climate-resilient Kuala Lumpur — a Sponge City that is better prepared for heavy rain and a changing climate,” she said.
Yeoh said the revamp is intended to go beyond beautification by creating a public space that better serves residents, strengthens the community and makes the city more liveable.
Medan Pasar, formerly known as Old Market Square, was one of Kuala Lumpur’s earliest commercial centres and remains a historic square anchored by its clock tower, built in 1937 to commemorate the coronation of King George VI.
The area is also among the key sites identified under Warisan KL, a national urban rejuvenation initiative aimed at breathing new life into Kuala Lumpur’s historic core through heritage and culture.
Creador Foundation has previously been involved in heritage-linked projects around Medan Pasar, including revitalising a corner lot in a row of old shophouses that included Sin Seng Nam, while its Muara Arts modern and contemporary arts centre is expected to open later this decade.
The latest project also dovetails with DBKL’s wider push to turn Kuala Lumpur into a “sponge city”, an urban model that Mayor Datuk Seri Fadlun Mak Ujud said in April was designed to better absorb rainwater, reduce flood risks and mitigate rising temperatures.

Title: Power outage at University station disrupts Kelana Jaya LRT services
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 13 — Kelana Jaya LRT services are experiencing delays this morning after a power outage at University station left a train unable to operate.
In a Facebook post, Rapid KL said alternative service arrangements have been activated, with trains travelling from Putra Heights and Gombak turning back at Asia Jaya.
As part of the disruption management, Platform 2 at Taman Bahagia and Taman Paramount stations has been temporarily closed for maintenance, while Platform 1 at Taman Jaya station is also closed.
Passengers at Taman Bahagia and Taman Paramount have been advised to use Platform 1 to board trains, while those at Taman Jaya should use Platform 2.
Commuters have been advised to take note of the temporary platform changes and allow additional time for their journeys.

Title: Unhealthy air quality recorded in 11 areas nationwide, Sarawak worst hit
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 13 — As of 9am today, air quality in 11 areas across the country is at unhealthy levels, with Sarawak reporting the most affected areas.
According to data from the Malaysian Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal, Samarahan registered the highest Air Pollutant Index (API) reading at 183, followed by Serian (182), Kuching (176), Sarikei and Sri Aman (158), while Mukah and Sibu each recorded readings of 152.
In Peninsular Malaysia, four areas posted unhealthy readings: Johan Setia (154) and Shah Alam (101) in Selangor, as well as Kuala Lumpur (131) and Putrajaya (104).
Meanwhile, 55 areas recorded moderate API readings of between 51 and 100, while two other areas registered good air quality below 50.
API readings from 0 to 50 indicate good air quality, 51—100 moderate, 101—200 unhealthy, 201—300 very unhealthy, and readings above 300 are classified as hazardous.
The API data is released hourly based on 68 air quality monitoring stations nationwide. — Bernama

Title: Seven areas in Sarawak record unhealthy API levels, down from nine
Article:
KUCHING, Aug 13 — Seven areas in Sarawak recorded unhealthy Air Pollution Index (API) readings due to transboundary haze as of 8am this morning, compared to nine areas yesterday morning.
Based on the Air Pollution Index Management System (APIMS), the areas recording unhealthy API readings are Samarahan (183), Serian (183), Kuching (177), Sri Aman (159), Sarikei (158), Mukah (152) and Sibu (152).
An API reading of zero to 50 indicates good air quality, 51 to 100 moderate, 101 to 200 unhealthy, 201 to 300 very unhealthy and an API above 300 is hazardous.
The API data is released hourly, based on 68 air quality monitoring stations nationwide. — Bernama

Title: Soldier suffers facial injuries after being accidentally shot during Port Dickson firing practice
Article:
SEREMBAN, Aug 13 — A soldier suffered facial injuries after being accidentally shot by a colleague at a firing range in Sungai Menyala, Port Dickson, yesterday.
Negeri Sembilan Police deputy chief SAC Mohd Nasharudin Mohd Shariff said the incident occurred at about 2.15pm when the victim, who is in his 20s, and several other personnel were taking part in a shooting practice.
“The victim was taken to Port Dickson Hospital before being transferred to Tuanku Ja’afar Hospital here for further treatment. He is reported to be in a stable condition,” he said in a statement today.
Following the incident, a man in his 20s, was detained under Section 37 of the Arms Act 1960 and Section 337 of the Penal Code to assist with investigations. — Bernama

Title: Former auditor-general says ‘right to be heard’ denied after not called to testify by Tabung Haji RCI
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 13 — Former Auditor-General Tan Sri Madinah Mohamad reportedly said she was disappointed she was not called to testify before the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) into Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH), despite turning up at the designated venue and being ready to give evidence.
Berita Harian
reported Madinah, who served as auditor-general from 2017 to 2019, as saying she was at the Department of Islamic Development Malaysia (Jakim) office on the appointed day and waited more than 30 minutes without being called.
“My right to be heard was denied when I was not called to testify in the proceedings, even though I had already turned up and waited there,” she was quoted as saying.
Madinah said she believed her right to be heard had been denied despite her attendance at the proceedings.
The 211-page RCI report said there had been a lack of firmness on the part of the auditor-general, noting that TH’s financial statements from 2014 to 2017 had received unqualified audit opinions, although the 2017 report included two Emphasis of Matter (EOM) paragraphs highlighting issues requiring attention.
Madinah defended her handling of the 2017 accounts, saying the EOMs were used to draw attention to material matters identified during the audit.
The RCI, however, found the issues warranted a qualified opinion, which would have formally signalled material problems with parts of the accounts.
Madinah said her decision was based on audit evidence and international auditing standards, arguing that a qualified opinion should not be issued unless the required criteria were met.

Title: Port Klang shophouse fire kills man and eight-year-old nephew, two others hospitalised
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Aug 13 — A 66-year-old man and his eight-year-old nephew died, while two others suffered breathing difficulties in a fire involving a three-storey shophouse on Jalan Batu Unjur 9, Taman Bayu Perdana, Port Klang this afternoon.
Selangor Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) assistant director of operations Ashrul Riezal Asbar said the department received an emergency call at 5.51pm and found the second floor of the Class A building, measuring about 20 x 70 square feet, 90 per cent damaged by the fire.
He said the two victims were believed to have been trapped when firefighters arrived, while the other two were rescued by members of the public and taken to Klang Hospital after suffering breathing difficulties.
“After the fire was extinguished, firefighters found the two victims in separate toilets at 6.33pm. Both were confirmed dead by Ministry of Health (MOH) personnel before their bodies were handed over to the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) forensics unit at 10.15pm,” he said in a statement yesterday.
He said the JBPM forensics team, together with the JBPM K9 Unit, conducted an initial investigation before the premises were handed over to the JBPM fire forensics team for further action.
The operation ended at 10.05pm, involving 18 personnel from the Port Klang and Andalas Fire and Rescue Stations. — Bernama

Title: RM10 a trip: GOF arrests Kelantan labourer who allegedly ferried undocumented migrants from river to bus station
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Aug 13 — For just a fee of RM10, a labourer allegedly moonlit as a transporter to ferry foreigners who entered Malaysia via un gazetted routes along Sungai Golok to a bus station.
The local man was arrested alongside an Indonesian man during Ops Taring Wawasan Kelantan by the Sector A Strike Force, Company A of the 7th Battalion (General Operations Force), near Gate 1 of the Rantau Panjang Duty-Free Complex, Pasir Mas at approximately 10pm on Tuesday.
PGA Southeast Brigade Commander SAC Ahmad Radzi Hussain said the arrest was made after personnel conducting patrols and monitoring spotted a red Demak 135 LC motorcycle ridden by two men acting suspiciously as they emerged from an illegal landing point area.
“Preliminary interrogation revealed that the local man lives around Rantau Panjang and works as a labourer, besides doing part-time work as a transporter charging a fee of RM10 to ferry customers, usually foreigners, who entered via the river to the bus station.
“An inspection of the Indonesian man, meanwhile, found that he did not possess an entry stamp into Malaysia and admitted to entering via Sungai Golok using an un gazetted route around Pengkalan Haram Azizah,” he said in a statement yesterday.
The Indonesian man was reported to have arrived at Hat Yai Airport, Thailand from Indonesia on August 10 before taking a bus to the Sungai Golok area to enter Malaysia, planning to continue his journey to Kuala Lumpur to meet a friend.
During the operation, the PGA also seized a Demak motorcycle registered under KEM 2321 valued at approximately RM4,000, two mobile phones, and a passport, with the total value of seizures estimated at RM6,000.
Ahmad Radzi said both men were handed over to the District Criminal Investigation Division of the Pasir Mas District Police Headquarters for investigation under Section 26J of the Anti-Trafficking in Persons and Anti-Smuggling of Migrants Act 2007, while initial urine screenings showed both were negative. — Bernama

Title: Anwar mourns Zhu Rongji, remembers ‘good friend’ who helped deepen Malaysia-China ties
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 13 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim yesterday expressed his condolences to the family of former Premier of the People’s Republic of China Zhu Rongji, who passed away at the age of 97.
Anwar described Zhu as one of the great architects of China’s economic transformation and a good friend, saying his reforms had helped accelerate the country’s rise as an economic superpower.
“China has lost one of the great architects of its economic transformation, and I have lost a good friend. It was Zhu’s reforms that helped accelerate China’s extraordinary rise as an economic superpower,” he said in a Facebook post yesterday.
Anwar said that in the 1990s, he and Zhu had worked together to deepen economic and financial ties between Malaysia and China, with much of what was built during that era continuing to underpin bilateral relations yesterday.
“In the 1990s, Zhu and I worked together to deepen economic and financial ties between Malaysia and China. Much of what we built in that era still underpins our relationship today,” he said.
Anwar also recalled personal memories of Zhu, including visits to Confucius’ home village, Tai Shan and historic sites associated with Admiral Zheng He, as well as a visit to his home library during which Zhu presented him with several Chinese classics he had personally selected.
“Zhu was a formidable statesman, but I will remember him above all as a man of great character, driven by a fierce sense of duty to his nation. My deepest condolences go to his wife, his children and to the people of China,” he said.
Zhu served as China’s Premier from 1998 to 2003 and was widely recognised for engineering major market-oriented reforms, restructuring state-owned enterprises, and steering the country’s entry into the World Trade Organisation (WTO). — Bernama

Title: Dr Mahathir, Dr Siti Hasmah recognised with three records after both turn 100
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 13 — Former Prime Minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad and his wife Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohd Ali have received three records recognising their longevity and unique achievements as a couple.
The 101-year-old Dr Mahathir was recognised by Asean Records as the Oldest Living Former Prime Minister, while 100-year-old Dr Siti Hasmah received the title of Oldest Living Spouse of a Former Prime Minister.
The couple also jointly received an ASIA Records recognition as the First Former Head of Government and Spouse to Both Become Living Centenarians.
In a Facebook post, Dr Mahathir said the recognition was presented at a ceremony held at the Perdana Leadership Foundation here Tuesday, marking a month of significant milestones for the couple.
Dr Mahathir celebrated his 101st birthday on July 10, followed by Dr Siti Hasmah’s 100th birthday on July 12. The couple also marked their 70th wedding anniversary on August 5.
The records’ adjudication team verified that no similar achievement has been publicly documented across the Asean region and major Asian markets.
Asean Records Advisory Board chairman Tan Sri Danny Ooi presented the certificates, accompanied by chief adjudicators Gillian Ooi and Eldrick Koh, who are also directors of Asean and ASIA Records. — Bernama

Title: Proposed Mara Bill to impose term limits on board members under governance overhaul, says chairman
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 13 — About 80 per cent of the proposed Majlis Amanah Rakyat (Mara) Bill 2026, to be tabled in Parliament before the end of the year, focuses on corporate governance aimed at strengthening the institution’s structure and management, said Mara chairman Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki.
In a Facebook post yesterday, he said that the move was intended to prevent further cases of abuse of power, governance weaknesses, misappropriation, irregularities, leakages and waste, as well as risks that could cause significant harm to the institution responsible for protecting the interests of Malays and Bumiputeras.
Asyraf Wajdi said a key provision in the Bill, which has been approved in principle by the Cabinet, involves reducing the powers of the Mara chairman to chairing the Board or Council and deciding on policy matters, compared with those currently provided under the Mara Act 1966.
“The Bill also provides for a separation of powers between the Board and Mara management, introduces ‘fit and proper’ criteria for Board members and limits their terms of service.
“The Bill will also tighten financial governance and procurement practices to ensure they meet national and international standards,” he said.
Asyraf Wajdi said the draft Bill would also establish several mandatory Board committees, including the Mara Audit, Investment, Finance and Governance, and Risk committees.
“The Bill will also establish a Syariah Committee for the first time to ensure all Mara operations adhere to Syariah principles,” he said, adding that the draft Bill includes several other important provisions on good governance that were not explicitly covered under the Mara Act 1966.
He said the new Bill was the culmination of governance reforms carried out since his appointment as Mara chairman on March 10, 2023, after he set up a special task force headed by former Bank Negara Malaysia governor Tan Sri Muhammad Ibrahim.
According to Asyraf Wajdi, the measures included strengthening financial discipline across Mara, carrying out forensic audits of its subsidiaries, centralising internal audit functions for Mara and Mara Corp, and restructuring the procurement division.
“Measures also included establishing a reporting system and introducing monthly financial performance reports for management to the Mara Council, in line with international standards,” he said.
On June 14, Asyraf Wajdi said the amendments to the Mara Act 1966 would ensure the new legislation was more relevant and better equipped to strengthen the agency’s role in advancing the Bumiputera development agenda. — Bernama

Title: ‘Back home’: PM Anwar discharged after hernia surgery
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 13 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim returned home yesterday after being discharged from hospital.
In a Facebook post, Anwar uploaded a photo of himself reading a book with the caption “Alhamdulillah, back home”.
Earlier, the Prime Minister’s wife, Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail, was reported to have said that Anwar was expected to be discharged from hospital yesterday after receiving treatment.
On Monday, Anwar was reported to have successfully undergone an elective laparoscopic surgical procedure to treat a para-umbilical hernia and was under close monitoring by a team of medical specialists. — Bernama

Title: When neutrality pays: How Malaysia is navigating the global fuel crisis
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 13 — With no end in sight, the war between the United States and Iran has left countries scrambling to shore up their fuel supplies and secure alternative sources of energy.
The Strait of Hormuz, a crucial route carrying about one-fifth of global oil and liquefied natural gas flows, has remained severely disrupted since the conflict erupted in late February.
Almost 40 per cent of Malaysia’s crude oil imports pass through the waterway, making any prolonged disruption a significant concern for the country’s energy security.
Malaysia, a net importer of crude oil, produces about 350,000 barrels of oil a day but consumes about 700,000 barrels, according to the Finance Ministry.
Malaysia also subsidises fuel for domestic consumption, keeping pump prices below those in some major oil-producing countries such as Saudi Arabia and Qatar.
Fuel subsidy spending surged from nearly RM800 million a month in January and February to around RM5 billion a month in March and April after global oil prices spiked following the outbreak of the war.
If high global oil prices persist, the country could face an overall fuel subsidy bill of about RM40 billion by the end of 2026.
Despite the pressure, Malaysia is turning the energy crunch into an opportunity to strengthen its diplomatic relationships, leveraging its long-held policy of neutrality and non-alignment.
Three developments illustrate how.
First, safe passage for Malaysian vessels through Hormuz
Malaysia maintains diplomatic relations with Iran despite their different political and sectarian orientations, while continuing to engage with Tehran through diplomatic channels.
On March 1, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim condemned the Israeli and US strikes against Iran, including the killing of Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei as “barbaric and illegal” and urged for an immediate ceasefire.
Those diplomatic ties proved useful when the energy crisis hit home.
Iran subsequently cleared seven Malaysian-owned vessels to transit the Strait of Hormuz for free due to Malaysia being a ‘friendly nation’, Transport Minister Anthony Loke told Bernama on March 31, citing Iran’s Ambassador to Malaysia Valiollah Mohammadi.
Malaysia again benefited from its diplomatic ties when a Petronas vessel sailing from Yanbu, Saudi Arabia, was cleared to transit the Red Sea in July, after the Iran-backed Houthis threatened to restrict passage through the Bab el-Mandeb Strait.
Anwar confirmed this on July 25 and said the Petronas-owned ship is slated to arrive in Melaka this month.
Second, securing longer-term supplies from friendly partners
Malaysia currently has sufficient fuel supplies and is working to secure longer-term stocks as the global energy crisis continues.
In doing so, the country is leveraging its broad diplomatic relationships with Russia and Central Asian countries to explore new energy sources and supply arrangements.
During Anwar’s maiden visit to Turkmenistan in June, national oil company Petronas secured rights to operate Blocks 9 and 10 in one of the country’s major gas-producing areas.
Petronas is expected to begin exploratory drilling there in December.
That same month, Russia pledged to provide Malaysia with long-term supplies of petrol, diesel and gas for at least 20 years, with the arrangement being finalised between the two countries.
The development comes as Malaysia continues its policy of non-alignment and has not joined Western sanctions against Russia over its invasion of Ukraine.
Third, using energy security to strengthen regional ties
Even as it navigates the energy crunch, Malaysia continues to maintain energy supply relationships with partners that are also seeking greater security amid global market uncertainty.
In June, Anwar announced that Petronas would supply up to two million tonnes of liquefied natural gas (LNG) a year to Japan’s largest power generation company, Jera, over a 20-year period starting in 2028.
Prior to that, he told his Australian counterpart Anthony Albanese in April that Malaysia would prioritise selling fuel surplus to Australia.
Anwar also said in June that Malaysia’s diesel surplus could be used to assist countries in need, including Timor-Leste, which became Asean’s 11th member last year.
Taken together, the developments underscore how Malaysia’s non-aligned foreign policy has given it room to maintain relationships across geopolitical divides while securing energy supplies and supporting regional partners during a period of heightened uncertainty.

Title: Tabung Haji RCI report to go to police, MACC, Bank Negara, IRB for full investigation, says Fahmi
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 12 — The Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) will go to the relevant authorities for a full investigation based on all findings and information contained in the report, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said.
He said the authorities included the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM), Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC), agencies responsible for matters under the Anti-Money Laundering, Anti-Terrorism Financing and Proceeds of Unlawful Activities Act (AMLA), Bank Negara Malaysia and the Inland Revenue Board (IRB).
“As a start, we will hand it over to the authorities as announced by the Prime Minister (Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim), whether the PDRM, MACC, AMLA, Bank Negara or IRB, to conduct a full investigation based on all the findings.
“This includes information contained in the report, as well as additional information provided by Finance Minister II (Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan) and Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan during the special Dewan Rakyat sitting on the Tabung Haji RCI report, yesterday.”
He said this to reporters after attending the Handover of Sponsorship Contributions for the 2026 National Day and Malaysia Day (HKHM) celebrations here today.
The TH RCI report was made public on July 29. It documented various management and operational weaknesses at TH between 2014 and 2020 and made 25 recommendations for improvement, 75 per cent of which had been implemented by TH as of July 30 this year.
Asked about calls by Barisan Nasional (BN) and Pakatan Harapan (PH) lawmakers for the government to establish a new TH RCI covering the 2021-2025 period, Fahmi, who is also Madani Government spokesman, said it would need the Cabinet and the King to decide.
“We all know that the decision to have the RCI was not only a Cabinet decision. As it is a Royal Commission of Inquiry, it also required the consent of the Yang di-Pertuan Agong,” he said.
Meanwhile, Fahmi described the attendance of Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (Bersatu) MPs at yesterday’s special Dewan Rakyat sitting to debate the TH RCI report as a wise and appropriate move.
He said this contrasted with other opposition parties in Perikatan Nasional (PN), which did not attend the debate.
“We must remember that this RCI was established in 2021 when PAS members and the Leader of the Opposition (Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainudin) were members of the Cabinet.
“But what I regret is that they did not attend the debate at all. They have missed a good opportunity.
“Perhaps...I am not sure, they were there when the RCI was initiated and when it completed its work, but they refused to attend the debate. What are they running away from?” he said.
Thirty-nine MPs debated the RCI report after Zulkifli presented his ministerial briefing on the matter at the special Dewan Rakyat sitting yesterday.
Some opposition MPs, however, staged a walkout from the Dewan Rakyat and boycotted the ministerial briefing and debate sessions after objecting to Speaker Tan Sri Johari Abdul’s decision to proceed without the presence of Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. — Bernama

Title: Two accused flee Kulim court, one slides down pillar to escape police
Article:
KULIM, Aug 12 — Two men attending a case mention at the Kulim Magistrate’s Court here today fled the court compound after spotting police officers waiting to re-arrest them in connection with another case.
Kulim police chief Supt Syamsul Sinring said the incident occurred at about 10am after both accused, aged 27 and 31, had completed their case mention and document submission.
He said both men were facing charges under Sections 324 and 353 of the Penal Code and had been granted bail pending trial after being charged at the same court on April 30.
“The first accused was granted bail of RM4,000 while the second was granted RM3,000. The case was fixed for re-mention on June 8, July 12 and today for document submission and case management,” he said in a statement today.
Syamsul said after completing the court proceedings, both men exited through the rear door before spotting police officers from the Seberang Perai Selatan (SPS) District Police Headquarters at the front entrance, who were there to re-arrest them in connection with another case.
“One of them immediately fled within the court compound and slid down a pillar from the first floor, while the other re-entered the building before escaping through the rear route.
“Both subsequently escaped by climbing over the rear fence,” he said, adding that police were working to locate the two men.
Earlier, a 24-second video went viral showing chaotic scenes at the Kulim Court Complex, in which a man believed to be one of the accused was seen climbing over a fence before fleeing. — Bernama

Title: Rubbish lorry crashes through Pantai Hillpark condo wall, crushes three cars
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 12 — A rubbish lorry believed to have suffered brake failure lost control and crashed into a condominium boundary wall, crushing three cars at Jalan Pantai Murni 1, Pantai Hillpark, early today.
Kuala Lumpur Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Department (JSPT) chief ACP Mohd Zamzuri Mohd Isa said the lorry was travelling downhill along a straight, sloping road when the incident occurred at about 4.10am.
He said the lorry veered off the road after its brakes failed, before coming down on three cars parked in the area.
The lorry driver, a 41-year-old local man, suffered an injury to his left leg, he said.
“The Kuala Lumpur JSPT immediately began efforts to locate the lorry driver after receiving the report, as he was not at the scene. He was successfully located while receiving treatment at Hospital Canselor Tuanku Muhriz, HUKM,” he said in a statement today.
Mohd Zamzuri said two Bangladeshi workers, both around 25, were carrying out rubbish collection work in the area when the incident occurred, but neither was injured as they were on the road at the time.
He said the lorry driver presented himself at the Kuala Lumpur Traffic Police Station at 3.15pm today to lodge a report on the incident.
“A breathalyser test found no alcohol in the driver’s system. The lorry will be sent to Puspakom for further examination to determine the exact cause of the incident,” he said, adding that the case is being investigated under Section 43(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987 for careless and inconsiderate driving. — Bernama

Title: Finance Ministry: Prices of non subsidised RON97, RON95, diesel cheaper by 20, 15 and 10 sen respectively from Aug 13 to 19
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 12 — The retail prices of non subsidised petroleum products for the period from August 13 to August 19, 2026, sees a drop, with RON97 down by 20 sen per liter, unsubsidised RON95 dropping by 15 sen, and unsubsidised diesel dropping by 10 sen.
According to a statement by the Ministry of Finance (MoF), for the stated period, the price of RON97 is set at RM4.15 per litre compared to RM4.35 previously, while unsubsidised RON95 is priced at RM3.62 per litre  compared to RM3.77, and unsubsidised diesel is set at RM4.47 per litre compared to RM4.57 previously.
At the same time, subsidised petroleum prices remain unchanged at RM1.99 per litre for RON95 under Budi Madani RON95 (Budi95) and RM2.10 per litre for diesel under Budi Madani Diesel (Budi Diesel).
MoF stated that the Madani Government shoulders a subsidy of RM1.63 per litre for eligible users under Budi95, equivalent to about 82 per cent of the RM1.99 per litre price paid at the pump while for Budi Diesel, a subsidy of RM2.37 per litre is borne, equivalent to about 113 per cent of the RM2.10 per litre price paid at the pump.
Prices for the Subsidised Petrol Control System (SKPS) and Subsidised Diesel Control Systems (SKDS) remain at RM2.05 and RM2.15 per litre , respectively.
In the meantime, MoF noted that the price drop follows the fall in global oil prices last week, when hopes for a resolution to the conflict between the United States and Iran caused global oil prices to trade at lower levels for most of the week.
Brent crude oil prices also dropped below US$80 (RM330) a barrel at the beginning of the Automatic Pricing Mechanism (APM) price calculation period, marking the lowest level in three weeks.
“However, geopolitical risk premiums rose again toward the end of the APM calculation period as prospects for negotiations between the United States and Iran deteriorated following new demands put forward by both parties,” according to the statement.
The ministry said Brent prices rose by nearly five per cent on Monday as concerns over the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz peaked again.
“Uncertainty regarding the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz continues to pose risks of global oil supply disruptions, thereby placing pressure on petroleum prices. Consequently, petroleum product prices are expected to continue experiencing significant fluctuations in the near future,” according to MoF. — Bernama

Title: Singapore fugitive flees to Johor, ends up kidnapped for S$80,000 ransom
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Aug 12 — A 32-year-old Singaporean wanted man, who fled to Johor for refuge, was instead kidnapped and assaulted before his family was blackmailed with a S$80,000 (about RM255,400) ransom.
Federal Criminal Investigation Department (CID) director Datuk M. Kumar said the victim, who is wanted by the Singapore police, had initially entered the country illegally at the end of May.
He said the victim was met by one of the six suspects in Johor Bahru shortly before his 28-year-old girlfriend also entered the country illegally.
“While the victim was in the midst of asking for assistance, he and his girlfriend were then kidnapped by the suspect.
“The suspects also forcefully took the victim’s cash consisting of S$12,000 and RM41,400.
“They then hatched a plan and demanded a S$80,000 ransom from the victim’s mother in Singapore,” he told reporters at the Johor police contingent headquarters here today.
Also present was Johor police chief Datuk Ab Rahaman Arsad and senior officers.
Following the ransom demand, Kumar said the victim’s mother then reported the matter to the Singapore Police Force (SPF) before investigators reached out to their Malaysian counterparts.
He said a Bukit Aman and Johor state CID task force was assembled to catch the suspects.
“While being detained, the male victim was deliberately slashed on both thighs before a photo of him was sent to his mother as a reminder of the ransom amount.
“As a result of negotiations, the male victim’s family and the suspect then agreed to a ransom sum of S$25,000, where S$5,000 was paid in advance online,” he said, adding that the remainder of the ransom was to be paid in cash during a meeting between the suspect and the victim’s family here.
Kumar said police then arrested a 40-year-old suspect during the ransom exchange held at a supermarket in Nusa Bestari, Iskandar Puteri at 6pm yesterday.
He said police also managed to rescue and free the two victims.
“Following that, police conducted a series of raids in Skudai and managed to arrest four men and a local woman, aged between 30 and 46, who are believed to be behind the kidnapping,” he said.
Checks showed that five of the six suspects had previous records involving criminal and drug offences. Four suspects also tested positive for methamphetamine abuse.
Kumar said police managed to recover the Singaporean and Malaysian currencies from the suspects that are believed to belong to the victim.
“This is in addition to house keys, mobile phones, jewellery, a Rolex watch and a Perodua Axia car with a total value of RM264,440.
“The motive for the kidnapping is still under investigation and police are actively tracking down other suspects who are still at large,” he said.
Kumar said the male victim was supposed to be under parole in Singapore, but fled and entered Johor illegally.
He said police believed that the victim’s contacts here had taken advantage of his situation to blackmail him.
The case is being investigated under Section 3(1) of the Kidnapping Act 1961, which is kidnapping for ransom.
The suspects have been remanded for 10 days starting today, while the two victims were also anrrested for illegally entering Malaysia.

Title: Five Chinese nationals arrested in Sri Petaling, Pudu over housebreakings in KL
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 12 — Five Chinese nationals suspected to have been involved in several housebreaking incidents in the capital were arrested in two separate raids in Sri Petaling and Pudu here on Sunday.
Kuala Lumpur Police Chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said investigations revealed that the suspects may have been involved in a housebreaking incident in Taman Desa Petaling on August 4, which caused the victim to suffer losses of about RM6,000 involving cash, jewelry, and a luxury-branded sling bag.
“During the raid at approximately 9.30pm, the police also seized a vehicle along with various tools used for housebreaking,” he said in a statement today.
Fadil said the police also recovered items belonging to the victim alongside various other luxury items including watches, wallets, and cash in various foreign currencies totalling more than RM10,000.
According to him, the suspects, aged between 38 and 58, are also believed to be involved in two other housebreaking cases around the Cheras area.
He said all suspects were remanded for four days starting Monday until tomorrow to assist with investigations under Section 457 of the Penal Code. — Bernama
